title: Stage 6 — Testing
goal: Add automated tests so refactors and deploys don't break your app silently.
summary: Unit tests for business logic, integration tests for HTTP endpoints, and a mindset for what to test first.

checkpoint.prompt: In a unit test, what does the "assert" step do?

choices.text: Checks the outcome matches what you expected
Sets up the database
Deploys to production

checkpoint.explanation: Arrange sets up inputs, act runs the code under test, assert verifies the result.

checkpoint.prompt: You want to test validation rules for creating a workout. Best layer to test directly?

choices.text: The service function — no HTTP server needed
Only the React button click handler
The CSS file

checkpoint.explanation: Service-layer unit tests are fast and pinpoint business rules without spinning up Express.

checkpoint.prompt: An integration test hits POST /workouts and expects 201. What is it verifying?

choices.text: The full HTTP stack: routing, middleware, handler, and response status
Only that JSON.parse works
That GitHub Actions is installed

checkpoint.explanation: Integration tests exercise real routes against a test app instance — closer to how clients call you.

checkpoint.prompt: Why write a test that POSTs invalid data and expects 400?

choices.text: So validation can't regress when someone refactors the route
Tests must only cover happy paths
400 responses don't matter in production

checkpoint.explanation: Sad-path tests lock in behavior you care about — especially API validation from Stages 3–4.

checkpoint.prompt: Tests run in GitHub Actions on every push. A test fails. What should happen to the PR?

choices.text: Merge is blocked until tests pass — fix or update the test intentionally
Merge anyway; tests are decorative
Delete the failing test

checkpoint.explanation: CI only helps when failing tests block broken code from landing on main.

checklist.label: Unit tests for at least one service/validation module
Integration tests for GET and POST on main resource
GitHub Actions (or CI) runs tests on push

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of automated tests in your project?

choices.text: Catch regressions when you change code
Replace manual coding entirely
Slow down development on purpose

questions.explanation: Tests document expected behavior and alert you when a change breaks it.

questions.prompt: Unit test vs integration test — which is faster and more isolated?

choices.text: Unit tests — they target one function without HTTP or DB
Integration tests — they always run faster
They are identical

questions.explanation: Unit tests avoid I/O. Integration tests hit the app stack and are slower but more realistic.

questions.prompt: For API integration tests, a common approach is to…

choices.text: Use a separate test database or in-memory DB, not production data
Always test against the live production database
Never touch a database in tests

questions.explanation: Tests must be repeatable and safe. Never run destructive tests against prod.

questions.prompt: Do you need test-driven development (write test first) to get value from tests?

choices.text: No — tests after code still catch regressions; TDD is optional
Yes — tests are useless unless written first
Yes — and you must achieve 100% coverage

questions.explanation: Some tests after the fact beat zero tests. Coverage targets are guides, not religion.

questions.prompt: For Track 1, where do tests give the most value first?

choices.text: API validation and endpoints — your contract with the frontend
Screenshot pixel diffs of every page
Testing only README spelling

questions.explanation: Backend tests stabilize the core. Frontend E2E comes later when flows are stable.
